title: Cummins Eyes South Africa ODIs as Launchpad for Historic Test Tour
excerpt: Australia captain plans to use three one-day internationals as match preparation before the first Test tour of South Africa since the 2018 ball-tampering scandal.
body:
• Pat Cummins plans to use Australia's three-match ODI series in South Africa starting September 24 as preparation for the high-stakes Test tour that follows.
  • Australia have not played a Test series in South Africa since the infamous 2018 ball-tampering scandal in Cape Town, making this tour emotionally and competitively charged.
  • The Test tour — three matches in Durban, Gqeberha and Cape Town from October 9–31 — is part of a gruelling 12-month stretch featuring up to 21 Tests, including a five-match series in India.
  • South Africa, the reigning World Test Championship holders, have been closely monitoring Australia's ageing pace attack after injuries disrupted the Bangladesh series.

Cummins Targets Full Workload Across Formats

Pat Cummins has signalled his intention to play Australia's three-match ODI series against South Africa in September as part of his build-up to the Test tour that follows — the team's first long-form visit to the country since the ball-tampering affair eight years ago.

Australia's Test and ODI captain has played just two ODIs since lifting the 50-over World Cup in 2023, and the September fixtures in Durban, Johannesburg and Potchefstroom offer rare competitive match time before the Tests begin on October 9.

"Body feels awesome. I got a scan, all sweet, so now it's the next step up, which is getting ready to bowl 20 overs in a day and wake up and do it again in a Test match."

— Pat Cummins, Australia captain

Cummins has been gradually increasing his bowling loads after a back injury curtailed his Ashes campaign earlier this year. He returned through the IPL with Sunrisers Hyderabad before rejoining Australia's Test squad for the Bangladesh series, where Mitchell Starc took 10 wickets in the second Test at Mackay to level the two-match series.

The Newlands Shadow Looms Large

The three-Test series carries weight beyond the World Test Championship standings. Several members of Australia's current squad — Cummins, Steve Smith, Starc, Nathan Lyon and Josh Hazlewood — were part of the 2018 touring party that produced one of cricket's most damaging controversies at Newlands.

David Warner and Cameron Bancroft, who received the heaviest sanctions, have since retired. But the return to Cape Town for the third Test on October 27 will inevitably revive painful memories. Australia played a T20I at Newlands in 2020, yet the format's brevity did not test the emotional significance the way a five-day match will.

Cricket South Africa revealed the full fixtures earlier this year, and officials on both sides have framed the tour as a marquee contest between the format's last two champions. South Africa won the inaugural World Test Championship final in 2023 and retain the title; Australia sit atop the current WTC standings.

South Africa Watching Australia's Pace Battery

The Proteas coaching staff have been closely monitoring Australia's fast-bowling stocks. Hazlewood did not play a Test in the Bangladesh series, while Cummins himself played only the first match. Scott Boland, 37, has emerged as a serious challenger for a permanent spot among the pace rotation.

"I know Scotty would never say it, but I think he's mounting a strong case that when you use the words 'the big three,' he could be one of those," Cricket Australia selector George Bailey told reporters ahead of the Bangladesh series.

Proteas coach Shukri Conrad has been studying both the Bangladesh and England–Pakistan series as he plots strategies for what he considers a defining home summer, according to reports from South Africa.

A 21-Test Marathon Ahead

The South Africa tour marks the second leg of an unprecedented 12-month stretch that will see Australia play up to 21 Tests. After the three Tests in South Africa, Cummins' squad will host New Zealand in a four-match home series beginning in December, followed by a five-Test tour of India in January–March 2027, a 150th anniversary Test against England at the MCG, and a possible WTC final before the Ashes in mid-2027.

For Indian cricket fans tracking Australia's progression, the South Africa tour will serve as a crucial form guide. How Cummins, Hazlewood and Starc manage their bodies across the ODIs and Tests in southern Africa will shape expectations for the India series barely three months later.

"I'm hoping that I play all of them, but I'm sure things will pop up along the way. It'd be very surprising if the same three bowlers played in 21 of the Tests."

— Pat Cummins

What to Watch

The first ODI is scheduled for September 24 at Kingsmead in Durban. The Test series begins on October 9 at the same venue before moving to St George's Park in Gqeberha and concluding at Newlands. Australia are also expected to play warm-up matches against Zimbabwe en route.
